report:
Reviewed the complete claim: checking an associated signature must (1) reuse its owning interface and (2) avoid reading sibling associated bodies. The owner alternatives are traits and impls; associated functions, types and constants are explicitly retained in the pending test matrix. There are three ordinary implementation entries and one TODO test, with no N/A entries.

The function implementation in local_syms/fns.rs calls open_owner before lowering the method signature. For a trait owner it calls local_trait.sig, imports that binder, uses its Self parameter and generics, inherits predicates and adds the owner trait predicate. For an impl owner it calls local_impl.sig and imports its generics, self type, predicates and optional implemented trait predicate. Method generics are appended after the owner generics, and owner_generic_count records the boundary. The no-owner branch creates an empty environment and is the non-associated case. Signature lowering checks parameter/return types and predicates without invoking body(); the separate body query consumes the signature, never the reverse.

The newly associated owner helpers in traits.rs and impls.rs are essential dependencies. Trait sig lowers its header generics, synthetic Self, predicates and eligibility; impl sig lowers its header generics, self type, optional trait reference and predicates. Neither traverses cst.items nor invokes an associated body. Owner items enumeration is a separate query. Unsupported header flags affect eligibility, not a fallback to sibling-body checking. These associations ensure future owner-helper edits invalidate this review.

Captured associated.rs explains the identity boundary: each selected item receives its owner, membership lookup examines names/kinds and copies the selected item's CST, and item enumeration exposes identities. This is structural parsing data, not an assertion that parsing never contains sibling body syntax. The claim concerns checking demand. Captured type_aliases.rs and consts.rs expose owner-bearing symbols but do not define general associated signature-checking queries; the specialized associated-type normalization path in impls.rs reuses impl.sig and selects a requested type value. This review does not claim a complete associated-type or constant signature implementation or dynamic dependency coverage.

The entire associated test set is sage_meta::todo::symbols_associated_interfaces. Its body has no assertions and explicitly requests a trace assertion excluding sibling-body reads for trait and impl functions, types and constants. It cannot detect regressions and is not treated as a passing behavioral test. Retaining this TODO is justified: closure requires fixtures that demand each supported associated signature, trace/assert owner-interface reuse, and reject sibling body dependencies; type/constant scenarios additionally require their signature paths. A plausible future regression, introducing a sibling body call into either owner helper or function sig, would require these trace assertions to detect it. Static inspection supports the implemented function/owner query separation but does not discharge this deferred test work. No reproduced behavioral defect was identified.

Executed review start/read commands and cargo fmt; no behavior suite was executed by this reviewer. The coordinator owns centralized tests, cargo build and delegated post-codegen/sanity checks for the two comment-only association edits. Fresh review inputs were captured after those edits. All inspected source dependencies supporting this assessment are captured. No further edits are requested; the explicit TODO remains deferred.
